PullRequest.Title: Add Azure SDK for C++ workspace tags
PullRequest.Body:
Revisits #197004 with a narrower, vcpkg-only implementation.

## Summary

- detect allowlisted Azure SDK for C++ packages from structured `vcpkg.json` dependencies
- support both string and object dependency forms
- detect use of the Azure SDK beta vcpkg registry from `vcpkg-configuration.json`
- add GDPR classifications for every emitted workspace tag
- add focused parser tests for malformed input, duplicate dependencies, false-positive package prefixes, and normalized registry URLs

This intentionally excludes CMake and `FetchContent` parsing to keep the telemetry source authoritative and the core workspace-tag implementation maintainable.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\tags\test\node\cppWorkspaceTags.test.ts`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- `npm run precommit`

Scenarios.Scenario: Local workspace startup telemetry resolves C++ vcpkg tags after workbench restoration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: WorkspaceTags is registered at LifecyclePhase.Eventually, which runs idle or after the 2.5-second fallback; editor startup and restoration do not await it. The workspace-tags telemetry event waits for root resolution plus all conditional manifest stats/reads and parsing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve each workspace root and enumerate its immediate children
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: R provider resolves in one resolveAll call
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same root enumeration already occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before any manifest-specific work and before the telemetry event can be emitted, but is off editor startup's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat and, when present, read vcpkg.json as text
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: If any root contains this filename, R stat calls plus M reads; otherwise zero calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No vcpkg.json stat or read was performed for workspace tags.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The workspace-tags telemetry promise waits for every call, but product UI startup does not.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat and, when present, read vcpkg-configuration.json as text
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: If any root contains this filename, R stat calls plus M reads; otherwise zero calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No vcpkg-configuration.json stat or read was performed for workspace tags.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The workspace-tags telemetry promise waits for every call, but product UI startup does not.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit the tags object through telemetry
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One event per window with at most 19 new constant-size boolean fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The telemetry event already existed; the PR only adds a constant-bounded set of possible fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs after tag resolution and is not awaited by UI progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Workspace-root count R, existing vcpkg manifest count M, manifest byte size B, and dependency count D. In the common single-root case, each present added filename causes one stat and one read; parsing is O(B + D).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Root resolution runs across all folders. For each added filename present in the aggregate root name set, getFilePromises starts one exists/stat per workspace root; both filename groups and all existing tag-file groups are then joined in one unbounded Promise.all. Reads begin after each successful stat.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The first getTags call performs the work and the completed Tags object is memoized in _tags; subsequent calls perform no filesystem or parse work. Missing files are effectively negative-cached only by that final Tags cache for the window lifetime. OS/provider caching is not relied on.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the added stat/read cardinality and scheduling from getFilePromises and Promise.all; low confidence that the bounded, eventual-phase work creates a material product impact.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Manifest sizes and root counts vary, but ordinary vcpkg manifests are small and most workspaces have few roots. The work runs after restoration, so there is no evidenced user-visible latency or throughput regression from the bounded added I/O.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The PR adds bounded filesystem work only for workspaces whose root listings contain the relevant filenames, and the work is off startup/UI critical paths.

Scenarios.Scenario: Remote or multi-root workspace performs vcpkg tag collection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The same Eventually-phase telemetry task waits for remote-provider stats and reads. Depending on the registered provider these calls can cross an IPC or network boundary, but no editor or user command awaits completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provider stat for each candidate vcpkg.json and vcpkg-configuration.json URI, followed by text read for matches
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero when neither name appears; otherwise R stats per appearing filename and M reads, all concurrent. Effective cardinality is by workspace root, not dependency item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These two filename-specific provider fan-outs did not exist; existing package-language tag checks retain their prior cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can delay only telemetry completion and consume provider capacity after restoration; it is not on interactive UI progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: R workspace roots and M roots containing each filename after aggregate-name gating. One matching filename anywhere causes a stat fan-out to all R roots; with both filenames present the diff can add up to 2R stats plus reads for each existing file.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All root-specific exists/stat promises for both filenames are launched without a limiter and joined with the existing manifest checks. There is no per-resource coalescing in this code, but the operation occurs once because getTags is cached.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold window execution performs provider calls; successful or absent results are retained indirectly in the final _tags cache for all warm calls. There is no repeated polling, invalidation, or retry loop.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the fan-out exists when aggregate name gating succeeds; lower confidence that it causes measurable contention because execution is delayed, one-shot, and normally low-cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The provider transport, latency, and prevalence of large multi-root C++ workspaces are not established. Very large R could create a burst, but no concrete user-visible contention is evidenced and realistic C++ workspace root counts are generally bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Although the diff adds up to two per-root stat groups on remote multi-root workspaces, the trigger is gated, one-shot, post-restoration telemetry work and lacks a concrete material impact.

Scenarios.Scenario: Parse vcpkg manifests and construct telemetry tag values
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Parsing occurs synchronously in each successful text-read continuation before the workspace-tags telemetry promise resolves; it is not on render, input, or startup restoration paths.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: JSON text bytes B and dependency/registry entries D. JSON.parse is O(B), dependency scanning is O(D) with constant-time map/set operations, registry scanning short-circuits, and emitted state is capped by the 18-package allowlist plus one registry tag.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One parser invocation per existing root manifest; invocations are scheduled by asynchronous file reads and do not spawn subprocesses or further boundary calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Parsed intermediate objects are released after resolution; only constant-bounded boolean tags remain in the memoized Tags object. No unbounded key retention or parser cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in linear parse/allocation cost and constant-bounded retained output.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Arbitrarily large JSON would increase synchronous parse time, but realistic vcpkg manifests/configurations are small and this PR neither buffers beyond the already-read file nor retains parsed input.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable serialization/allocation or retention issue; work is linear, one-shot per manifest, and output cardinality is capped.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and traced the only product path through Eventually-phase workspace telemetry. The diff adds gated, one-shot vcpkg file stats/reads and linear parsing, including per-root remote-provider fan-out, but does not place work on startup or interaction critical paths and does not establish a material user-visible regression. No findings were submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
